etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English mone, from Old English mōna (“moon”), from Proto-West Germanic *mānō, from Proto-Germanic *mēnô (“moon”), from Proto-Indo-European *mḗh₁n̥s (“moon, month”), probably from *meh₁- (“to measure”).

definitions.definition: (informal, by extension of Moon) Any natural satellite of a planet.
(literary) A month, particularly a lunar month.

quote.text: For since these arms of mine had seven years' pith,Till now some nine moons wasted, they have usedTheir dearest action in the tented field…

quote.citation: 1737, John Brickell, The natural history of North-Carolina, pages 308–309:
quote.text: They number their age by Moons or Winters, and say a Woman or a Man is so many Moons old, and so they do with all memorable Actions in life, accounting it to be so many Moons or Winters since such or such a thing happened.

quote.citation: 1822, Thomas Love Peacock, Maid Marian, page 238:
quote.text: Many moons had waxed and waned when on the afternoon of a lovely summer day a lusty broad-boned knight was riding through the forest of Sherwood.

quote.citation: 2002, Russell Allen, "Incantations of the Apprentice", on Symphony X, The Odyssey.
quote.text: Through eerie reach of ancient woods / Where lumbering mists arise / I journey for nines moons of the year / To where a land of legend lies

definitions.definition: A representation of the moon, usually as a crescent or as a circle with a face; a crescent-shaped shape, symbol, or object.
A crescent-like outwork in a fortification.
The eighteenth trump/major arcana card of the Tarot.
(card games) In hearts, the action of taking all the point cards in one hand.
(transitive, colloquial) To display one's buttocks to, typically as a jest, insult, or protest.
(intransitive, colloquial) To gaze at lovingly or in adoration.

quote.citation: 1938, Norman Lindsay, Age of Consent, 1st Australian edition, Sydney, N.S.W.: Ure Smith, published 1962, →OCLC, page 164:
quote.text: Bradly stood bewitched, mooning at the moon. Betimes he bent in a grotesque posture and looked at it between his legs, which was to rid his mind of preconceived colour values by seeing them upside down.

definitions.definition: (intransitive, colloquial) (usually followed by over or after) To fuss over something adoringly; to be infatuated with someone.

quote.citation: 2017 January 12, Jesse Hassenger, “A literal monster truck is far from the stupidest thing about Monster Trucks”, in The Onion AV Club‎[1]:
quote.text: On some level, the filmmakers behind Monster Trucks must have recognized the ill fit of Till playing a teenager, because they cast Jane Levy, a 27-year-old who can pass for younger but not a decade younger, as Meredith, a nerdy classmate of Tripp’s who moons over him as she insists on making an appointment to tutor him in biology.

quote.citation: 2023 September 24, HarryBlank, “Working Wonders”, in SCP Foundation‎[2], archived from the original on 25 May 2024:
quote.text: "No, you're right." Udo shook this newest distraction out of her head. She knew it would come creeping back in through the ears in due time, just as she knew the best way to dispel it was to finish the job and link up with the rest of the Site. In any event, there was something in what Brenda had said that didn't make sense... "But why would he be mooning over her, if she's still awake?""Because he's with V—""Veiksaar!" Udo fairly shouted, slapping her forehead. "Oh, shit. This is going to take a lot of getting used to."
We were only three on board. The poor old skipper mooned in the cabin.

quote.citation: 2001, Stephen King, The Death of Jack Hamilton:
quote.text: I mooned around. I was mighty sick of the room by then.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To expose to the rays of the Moon.
(transitive) To adorn with moons or crescents.
(cryptocurrencies, of a coin or token) To rise in price rapidly or suddenly.

quote.citation: 2019, Mark Grabowski, Cryptocurrencies: A Primer on Digital Money‎[3], Routledge, →ISBN:
quote.text: I've followed several of the most popular crypto pundits on Twitter and discovered they constantly brag about their one big Hail Mary pick that mooned but neglect to mention – or delete – their numerous fumbles.
